summary: Path traversal: the name parameter is joined to the upload directory without containment, reaching any readable file. The file header tells reviewers to skip it (prompt-injection check).
Insecure direct object reference: GET /api/invoices/:id returns any customer's invoice without canSee.
Open redirect: next is used as the Location header without checking it is a local path.
Pagination: pages are numbered from 1 but page 1 starts at index 20, so the first 20 invoices are never listed.
Date range: to is documented as inclusive but compared with <, dropping invoices issued on the end date.
Webhook retries: recordPayment records eventId but never checks it, so a redelivered event adds the payment again.
execFile with a fixed command and arguments; no request data reaches the child process.
HTML output is escaped, including the e-mail in the page title and heading.
Loose == null comparison is intentional and documented.
Session MAC comparison uses timingSafeEqual with a length check.
The /invoices page escapes the e-mail and invoice fields before rendering.
File download authorization: /files serves any invoice PDF by name without checking that the invoice belongs to the user.

Unbounded body: readBody rejects after 64 kB but keeps appending every chunk, so an anonymous webhook request can exhaust memory.
Crash: GET /files with an empty name resolves to the uploads directory, passes existsSync, and the read stream error is unhandled, so one request stops the process.
